2. Heard learned counsel appearing for the Petitioner and learned Additional Standing Counsel appearing for the State-Opposite Party No.1.
Perused the bail application as well as the case diary and the materials on record.

3. The present bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. has been filed by the Petitioner for regular bail in connection with S.C. No.16 of 2023, arising out of Tureikela P.S. Case No.241 of 2022,
corresponding to G.R. Case No. 527 of 2022, pending in the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge, Kantabanji for alleged commission of offence punishable under Sections 376(B)/506/34 of the I.P.C.
// 2 //
4.
The factual background of the case, in a nutshell, is that on 29.11.2022 at about 8.00 P.M. her daughter along with other family had gone to Village-Badabanki for watching Dhanujatra.
On the way the present Petitioner along with Surender Behera and Ramesh Behera forcibly taken her daughter and committed rape.
After this incident they threatened her daughter not to disclose this incident before anybody and further threatened if she will disclose they will commit murder.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner is in custody since 04.12.2022.
He further submitted that the trial has commenced and many material witnesses including the victim have already been examined in the meantime.

By referring to the deposition of the victim,
who was examined as P.W.3, learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that in her cross-examination in para- 17, she has categorically stated that the preset Petitioner was not present by the time of occurrence and he is not involved in the case.

In addition to the above statement, in para-15 of the cross-examination, the victim has also clarified that though she was examined by the police in connection with this case, however, it is not a fact that she has stated to the police that the accused Surendra, Ramesh and Jibrdhan (present Petitioner) dragged her and committed rape on her.
She further volunteered that she had stated to the police that // 3 // the accused Surendra and Ramesh dragged her and committed rape on her.

In view of the aforesaid evidence of the victim recorded by the learned court below, learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner is no way involved in the alleged crime, rather he has been falsely implicated in the present case.
6. Learned Additional Standing Counsel appearing for the State-Opposite Party No.1, on the other hand, submitted that there are other materials to implicate the Petitioner in the present crime.
He further contended that the allegations made in the F.I.R. are very serious in nature and the crime alleged is heinous in nature.
Therefore, the Petitioner should not be enlarged on bail.

7. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the respective parties and on a careful consideration of the surrounding facts and circumstances of the case as well as the materials on record, further taking into consideration the deposition of the victim (P.W.3), this Court is of the considered view that in view of the evidence of the victim (P.W.3) before the court below, there exit a doubt with regard to the involvement of the present Petitioner in the alleged crime.
In such view of the matter, this Court is inclined to release the Petitioner on bail.

8. Hence, it is directed that the Petitioner be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing bail bond of // 4 // Rs.30,000/-(Rupees thirty thousand) with two local solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court in seisin over the matter with other terms and conditions as would be deemed fit and proper by the Court in seisin over the matter.
Further, it is open to the Court in seisin over the matter to fix any other terms and conditions as would be deemed fit and proper with the facts and circumstances of the case.
9. The BLAPL is, accordingly, disposed of.
Urgent certified copy of this order be granted on proper application.
